notes.text: WHO duration by indication: at least 10 days for suspected sepsis, at least 3 weeks for suspected meningitis, at least 7 days for suspected pneumonia.

notes.text: WHO: give ampicillin plus a third-generation cephalosporin plus gentamicin if Listeria is suspected.

notes.text: FDA label: in the neonate with suspected sepsis a penicillin-type drug is usually also given.
notes.quote: In the neonate with suspected bacterial sepsis or staphylococcal pneumonia, a penicillin-type drug is also usually indicated as concomitant therapy with gentamicin.

notes.text: Aminoglycosides need caution in premature and neonatal infants because of renal immaturity.

bands.label: Pediatric patients older than 1 week
bands.quote: Pediatric Patients (Greater Than 1 Week of Age): 6 to 7.5 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equally divided doses (2 to 2.5 mg/kg every 8 hours or 1.5 to 1.89 mg/kg every 6 hours).

bands.label: Pediatric patients older than 1 week, 6-hourly option

notes.text: Infusion shorter than 20 minutes is not recommended.
notes.quote: The diluted solution usually should be infused over a period of 20 to 60 minutes. Infusion periods of less than 20 minutes are not recommended because peak serum levels may exceed 12 mcg/mL

regimens.indication: Neonates up to 1 month (FDA label)

bands.label: Initial dose
bands.quote: In neonates, an initial dose of 15 mg/kg is suggested, followed by 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for neonates in the 1st week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to the age of 1 month. Each dose should be administered over 60 minutes.

bands.label: Maintenance, 1st week of life
bands.quote: In neonates, an initial dose of 15 mg/kg is suggested, followed by 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for neonates in the 1st week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to the age of 1 month. Each dose should be administered over 60 minutes.

bands.label: Maintenance, after 1st week up to 1 month
bands.quote: In neonates, an initial dose of 15 mg/kg is suggested, followed by 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for neonates in the 1st week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to the age of 1 month. Each dose should be administered over 60 minutes.

notes.text: Premature infants: clearance falls as postconceptional age falls; longer dosing intervals may be needed and serum concentration monitoring is recommended.
notes.quote: In premature infants, vancomycin clearance decreases as postconceptional age decreases. Therefore, longer dosing intervals may be necessary in premature infants. Close monitoring of serum concentrations of vancomycin is recommended in these patients.

notes.text: HHS: NVP dosing for GA 32 to under 37 weeks is not FDA approved; doses for GA 32 to under 34 weeks are model-based and might underestimate toxicity.

notes.text: HHS: do not use NVP if HIV-2 infection is present or suspected.
notes.quote: Do not use NVP if HIV­2 infection (or HIV-2 co-‍infection with HIV-1) is present or suspected

regimens.indication: Premature newborns (FDA label; dose in mg/kg as for older children)

bands.label: Premature GA 26 to 29 wk, first two weeks of life (interval only)
bands.dose_note: same mg/kg as older children; the label gives no separate neonatal mg/kg figure
bands.quote: Based on the prolonged half-life seen in premature newborns (gestational age 26 to 29 weeks), these children, in the first two weeks of life, should receive the same dosage (mg/kg) as in older children, but administered every 72 hours. After the first two weeks, these children should be dosed once daily.

bands.label: Premature GA 26 to 29 wk, after the first two weeks (interval only)
bands.quote: Based on the prolonged half-life seen in premature newborns (gestational age 26 to 29 weeks), these children, in the first two weeks of life, should receive the same dosage (mg/kg) as in older children, but administered every 72 hours. After the first two weeks, these children should be dosed once daily.

notes.text: No pharmacokinetic information in full-term newborns.
notes.quote: No information regarding fluconazole pharmacokinetics in full-term newborns is available.

regimens.indication: Candidemia, acute disseminated candidiasis, Candida peritonitis and abscesses WITHOUT meningoencephalitis or ocular dissemination, under 4 months (FDA label)

bands.label: Younger than 4 months
bands.quote: 2.3 Dosage for Pediatric Patients Younger than 4 Months of Age Treatment of Candidemia, Acute Disseminated Candidiasis, Candida Peritonitis and Abscesses without meningoencephalitis and/or ocular dissemination The recommended dosage is 4 mg/kg once daily.

notes.text: Not established for candidemia with meningoencephalitis or ocular dissemination under 4 months; a higher dose may be needed.
notes.quote: The safety and effectiveness of micafungin for injection have not been established for the treatment of candidemia with meningoencephalitis and/or ocular dissemination in pediatric patients younger than 4 months of age as a higher dose may be needed

regimens.indication: Treatment of influenza, 2 weeks to under 1 year (FDA label)

bands.label: 2 weeks to under 1 year
bands.quote: Pediatric patients 2 weeks to less than 1 year of age: 3mg/kg twice daily for 5 days

notes.text: Treatment is labelled from 2 weeks of age; prophylaxis only from 1 year.
notes.quote: Administer Oseltamivir Phosphate for the treatment of influenza in patients 2 weeks of age or older [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.2 )] or for prophylaxis of influenza in patients 1 year and older

regimens.indication: Pertussis treatment or postexposure prophylaxis, infants under 6 months incl. neonates (CDC 2005)

bands.label: Infants under 6 months
bands.quote: It is administered as a single daily dose. Recommended regimen: Infants aged <6 months: 10 mg/kg per day for 5 days.

notes.text: CDC: azithromycin is the preferred macrolide under 1 month; monitor for infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.
notes.quote: Monitor infants <1 month of age who receive a macrolide for the development of IHPS and for other serious adverse events.

regimens.indication: Pertussis, infants under 1 month ONLY if azithromycin is unavailable (CDC 2005)

bands.label: Under 1 month (azithromycin unavailable)
bands.quote: Recommended regimen: Infants aged <1 month: not preferred because of risk for IHPS. Azithromycin is the recommended antimicrobial agent. If azithromycin is unavailable and erythromycin is used, the dose is 40--50 mg/kg per day in 4 divided doses.

regimens.indication: Prophylaxis of neonatal gonococcal or chlamydial ophthalmia (FDA label)

bands.label: Newborn, each eye
bands.freq: once, into each lower conjunctival sac
bands.quote: For prophylaxis of neonatal gonococcal or chlamydial ophthalmia, a ribbon of ointment approximately 1 cm in length should be instilled into each lower conjunctival sac.

notes.text: CDC: increased risk of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in neonates after erythromycin; monitor.
notes.quote: An increased risk for IHPS has been reported in neonates during the month after erythromycin administration.

notes.text: Ophthalmic ointment should not be flushed from the eye; use a new tube for each infant.
notes.quote: The ointment should not be flushed from the eye following instillation. A new tube should be used for each infant.

notes.text: No neonatal dose in the label: safety and effectiveness below 1 month of age not established.
notes.quote: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients below the age of one month have not been established

notes.text: Lower concentrations may suit infants and small children to give enough infusion volume.
notes.quote: Lower concentrations (0.2 mg/mL to 0.5 mg/mL) may be appropriate for infants and small children to provide sufficient volume for infusion.

notes.text: No neonatal dose in the label; pediatric use should be limited to the smallest effective dose.
notes.quote: Amphotericin B for Injection when administered to pediatric patients should be limited to the smallest dose compatible with an effective therapeutic regimen.
